correctness.rationale: The bipartite stable-set inequalities are all facet-defining by total unimodularity and degree>=3. The scalar trace root is unique by spectral monotonicity with 0 and 2d eigenvalues and Jensen/chord bounds. Vertex/edge transitivity makes two facet-support norms constant; the root forces every slack equal to its corresponding ellipsoid radius. Explicit positive weights 2/(r+2) per coordinate and 2r/[d(r+2)] per edge satisfy the exact John centroid/covariance identities, proving global maximality and uniqueness. The H spectrum and second trace moment tr[(H/d-I)^2]/N=1/d yield the strict semiaxis bracket and universal large-degree limit. Newly constructed 3-cube verifies Q_ii=a², each edge norm=b² and John matrix equality to 3.6e-15; finite check is corroboration only.

value.rationale: The explicit metric maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid on stable-set polytopes of a natural infinite symmetry family is not just an optimized example. A universal signless-Laplacian prescription, exact all-facet contacts, and an unusual graph-independent high-degree limiting eccentricity reveal structural geometry with plausible use for further graph-polytope metric questions.

final_claim: For any finite connected simple vertex-and-edge-transitive bipartite graph of degree d>=3, the vertex-space stable-set polytope has a unique fully tangent signless-Laplacian John ellipsoid with uniquely defined scalar root and squared-semiaxis ratio in (1+sqrt(2),3) tending to 1+sqrt(2) as degree grows.
limitations: Requires connected simple bipartite graphs with both vertex and edge transitivity and degree>=3. Spectral root need not be radical.
